atlas-au.0128: For an employer that does sponsor, the Core Skills stream requires the occupation to be on the list, at least one year of relevant experience, a salary at the market rate and at least A$79,499, and the employer must be an approved sponsor and nominate the position; a new graduate usually does not meet the experience test.
atlas-au.0129: The 2025 survey reports that 22.8% of international postgraduates in jobs not fully using their education cite the lack of permanent residency as the main reason, so state your work rights early.
atlas-au.0130: Boards and portals: GradConnection (SEEK Grad), Workforce Australia (the government service), the APS Jobs graduate pages, LinkedIn, and recruiters such as Michael Page, which lists a graduate programme.
atlas-au.0131: Employer pages carry the programmes and dates: Macquarie, KPMG, Commonwealth Bank, Atlassian and ASD; university career centres run graduate job and internship fairs, such as Sydney’s on 5 March 2026.
atlas-au.0132: The Australian Association of Graduate Employers (aage.com.au) publishes the employer, candidate and graduate surveys cited here and lists events.
atlas-au.0133: Applying in the final semester: 50% of graduates start before their final year, internship rounds close in July and August for the summer, and Macquarie’s graduate round for February 2027 closed on 13 October 2026.
atlas-au.0134: Sending a European CV: a photo, date of birth or marital status is advised against by UNSW, and three pages is for extensive experience or research output only.
atlas-au.0135: Applying to a citizens-only programme: the federal programme and ASD need Australian citizenship, so international applicants should target employers that say they accept them.
atlas-au.0136: Assuming a master’s fixes the gap: international business postgraduates were in full-time work at 53.3% against 92.2% for domestic graduates in 2025.
atlas-au.0137: The bank and investment-bank programmes read (Commonwealth Bank, Macquarie) are in English and state no other language requirement.
atlas-au.0138: The Big Four graduate programmes run in English; the KPMG listing asks for a degree in accounting, finance, commerce, economics or data and states no language level.
atlas-au.0139: Federal programmes require citizenship and run in English; the pages read name no language test.
atlas-au.0140: Atlassian’s graduate software programme in Sydney is in English and does not sponsor visas.
atlas-au.0141: ASD’s Cyber stream is in English and needs citizenship and a Positive Vetting clearance.
atlas-au.0142: QILT 2025 puts full-time employment at 50.8% for international undergraduates and 52.2% for international postgraduate coursework graduates, against 75.4% and 88.3% for domestic graduates; the methodology changed in 2025 and the figures are not directly comparable with earlier years.
atlas-au.0143: Employers say graduates stay: 76% expect to stay 3 years or more, and 89% say their programme is better than expected.
atlas-au.0144: No return-offer rate from internship to graduate programme was found in the pages read, beyond Macquarie’s note that interns can be fast-tracked.
atlas-au.0146: A CRICOS course issues a Confirmation of Enrolment; you must pass the Genuine Student test and hold student health cover (OSHC) for the whole visa. The European health card does not replace OSHC.
atlas-au.0147: Up to 48 hours per fortnight in term, unlimited in breaks; research degrees have no limit. Since July 2024 you cannot apply onshore from a visitor or graduate visa.
atlas-au.0148: AUD 29,710 a year, plus tuition and travel
atlas-au.0150: An unpaid placement is legal only if your course requires it for credit; any other internship makes you an employee owed the minimum wage. A sponsor can bring you on a 407 training visa, up to two years with a structured plan.
atlas-au.0155: After at least two academic years of study in Australia: two years for a bachelor’s or coursework master’s, three for research degrees. Apply in Australia within six months of completing, aged 35 or under (50 for research degrees), with IELTS 6.5.
atlas-au.0157: An approved sponsor nominates the role: the Specialist stream for high salaries in any skilled job, the Core stream for jobs on the Core Skills Occupation List. A year of experience and IELTS 5.0; after two years with the sponsor, permanent residence through the 186.
atlas-au.0158: British citizens skip labour-market testing under the UK–Australia trade agreement; EU citizens do not.
atlas-au.0163: If the job ends you have 180 days to find a new sponsor, and may work meanwhile.
atlas-au.0165: Subclasses 189, 190 and 491 need a skills assessment, competent English and an invitation through SkillSelect. The legal minimum is 65 points, but invitations in 2026 went to 85 to 95 or more. EU citizens must sit an English test; British citizens are deemed competent.
atlas-au.0168: Students of foreign universities invited to a research project can come on a 408 visa, up to 12 months, with no enrolment or tuition.
atlas-au.0169: PhD students may work without limit, and so may their partners; Research Training Program scholarships cover fees with a tax-free stipend.
atlas-au.0173: Italy, France, Germany, Ireland, Denmark, Finland, Sweden, Cyprus and the UK have the 417 up to age 35; Belgium, Estonia, Malta and the Netherlands up to 30. Spain, Portugal, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia, Greece and Austria use the 462, which needs two years of university and basic English.
atlas-au.0174: A second and third year need 88 days and then six months of regional work, except for British citizens, exempt since July 2024.
atlas-au.0176: Pay slips are cross-checked with the tax office: unpaid or false regional work leads to refusal and a ban.
atlas-au.0178: EU and UK citizens get a free eVisitor, valid 12 months, for visits of up to three months each, with no work.
atlas-au.0179: Apply online through ImmiAccount. Documents not in English need a translation by a NAATI-accredited translator.
atlas-au.0180: If Home Affairs gives you a health examination ID (HAP ID), book the medical with an approved panel physician: in Italy only in Rome and Milan, typically €180 to €300.
atlas-au.0181: Students on a 500 visa must hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the whole visa; holders of temporary work or visitor visas without Medicare need Overseas Visitor Health Cover (OVHC).
atlas-au.0182: Australian visas are digital and linked to your passport; there is no residence card to collect. Students then create their Unique Student Identifier (USI) online after landing: without it the university cannot issue results or degrees.
atlas-au.0183: Apply online for a Tax File Number from the ATO, free, but only once you are in Australia: if your employer does not have it within 28 days of hiring, it must withhold 45% of your pay.
atlas-au.0184: Your employer pays 12% of ordinary pay into a superannuation fund, which follows you from job to job.
atlas-au.0185: Italian citizens can enrol in Medicare in person at Services Australia under the reciprocal health care agreement, with passport, visa and Italian health card, on form MS015: the card lasts up to 6 months and covers urgent public care and GP visits. It does not exempt students on a 500 visa from OSHC.
atlas-au.0186: Students must keep OSHC for the whole visa; check with Services Australia what other cover applies to you.
atlas-au.0187: A valid application made in Australia gives you a Bridging Visa A, which keeps you lawful after your visa expires but has no travel rights: leaving cancels it. To travel and return, first get a Bridging Visa B (AUD 575).
atlas-au.0188: If an application is refused while you are on a bridging visa, you can apply for almost no other visa from inside Australia (section 48 bar).
atlas-au.0189: A Bridging Visa A has no travel right: leave Australia while waiting and it ends at the border. To travel you need a Bridging Visa B first.
atlas-au.0190: A refusal while on a bridging visa triggers the Section 48 bar: you can apply for almost nothing more from inside Australia.
atlas-au.0191: Give your employer a tax file number within 28 days, or 45% is withheld.
atlas-au.0192: Working holidaymakers pay 15% from the first dollar, and 65% on the pension savings they take home when they leave.
atlas-au.0193: The Essential Skills stream for lower-paid care work is not yet fully running.
atlas-au.0194: Enrolment caps per provider hit private colleges harder than the Group of Eight universities.
atlas-au.0195: Applying for a student visa offshore right after a visitor or graduate visa ends draws strict scrutiny.
